title: Ark of the Covenant as a device that strikes people dead with fire

tellings.quote: according to the the Book of Exodus. But also, it strikes people dead with bolts of fire that come out of it.
And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer, and put fire therein, and put incense thereon, and offered strange fire before the LORD, which he commanded them not.
And there went out fire from the LORD, and devoured them, and they died before the LORD.

And the LORD said unto Moses, Speak unto Aaron thy brother, that he come not at all times into the holy place within the vail before the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not: for I will appear in the cloud upon the mercy seat.

plain: The writer Graham Hancock says on the show that, according to the Book of Exodus, the Ark of the Covenant, the sacred chest the Israelites carried through the desert, "strikes people dead with bolts of fire that come out of it." No verse in the books of Moses in the King James Bible, published in 1611, says fire comes out of the Ark. The closest passage tells how Aaron's sons offered "strange fire" and "there went out fire from the LORD, and devoured them," and Aaron is warned to keep away from "the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not." The deaths at the Ark itself come later, in the books of Samuel, where a man named Uzzah "died by the ark of God" and the men of Bethshemesh were struck down for looking inside it, and neither passage mentions fire.

discussion.by: The King James Version of the Bible
discussion.text: The books of Moses tell of a deadly holiness about the Ark: when Aaron's sons offered strange fire, "there went out fire from the LORD, and devoured them" (Leviticus 10:2), and Aaron is warned to keep from "the mercy seat, which is upon the ark; that he die not" (Leviticus 16:2). The books of Samuel, which name no author, tell of deaths at the Ark itself: Uzzah, who "died by the ark of God" when God "smote him" (2 Samuel 6:7), and the men of Bethshemesh smitten "because they had looked into the ark of the LORD" (1 Samuel 6:19). So a deadly Ark is in the text, and so is fire from the LORD; the passages are in Leviticus and Samuel where the teller names Exodus, and joining the two into fire coming out of the Ark itself is the teller's step, which the text neither states nor excludes.
